Function class: M1-F1 Genome defence / self-marking
Candidate function: Modification of the recognition sequence marks the host genome as self and protects it from the cell's own sequence-specific defence system
Evidence: **[2026-10-06 Second revision. Occupancy alone cannot reject the 4mC shield hypothesis]** Initially, all three marks were rejected on the grounds that 'the level distribution is unimodal and does not saturate, so it cannot function as a shield', but in light of the measured methylome from REBASE v610 (Q1_occupancy_by_chemotype_and_system_261006.csv), two confounds have come to light. (1) **Coverage depth strongly confounds occupancy.** The median occupancy of RM-system-associated motifs for m4C is 79.6% at 0-58x / 93.7% at 58-90x / 98.2% at 90-147x / 96.8% at 148-769x. The m4C median of 87.7% (n=993) pooled across all coverage is a value dragged down by low coverage. (2) **Orphan status does not predict partial modification.** Orphan MTases for m6A (n=579) have a median occupancy of 99.4%, a mean of 97.02%, and only 0.52% below 50%, making them **if anything more complete** than RM-system-associated ones (n=8,672, median 99.0%, 2.42% below 50%). Therefore, the explanation derived from Blow 2016 that 'partial modification is the hallmark of an orphan MTase' is not supported by REBASE's own measured data (this point corrects my own report earlier in this session). Position within a population controlled for coverage >=90x: TGGCCGGC 4mC 90.11% is at the **23.4th percentile** of RM-system-associated m4C (n=244, median 97.3%), and AAGCCCG 4mC 76.69% is at the 11.1th percentile. Meanwhile, AAGCCCG 6mA 45.84% is at the **1.03rd percentile** of RM-system-associated m6A (n=3,601, median 99.5%) and the **0.52nd percentile** of orphan m6A (n=579). Whichever population is chosen, 6mA is an extreme outlier. **Conclusion: for 4mC, occupancy alone cannot reject the shield hypothesis (Undecidable with these data). For 6mA, it can be rejected.** The substantive argument on the 4mC side is not occupancy but the absence of a candidate cognate REase for TGGCCGGC (BREX-2 PglX is 6mA-type across all subtypes, so it cannot be the enzyme for TGGCCGGC). Direct comparator: the only known enzyme that places 4mC at position 3 of GCCGGC is the single case M.PfrJS2V (Propionibacterium freudenreichii JS2, 415 aa, Type II alpha, host genome GC 67.2%, doi:10.1186/s12864-017-4165-9 PMID 29037147). **This itself is an orphan with no cognate REase, a partial modification at 58.7% occupancy (141.5x coverage)**, whereas all four 6mA enzymes in the same strain are at 100% (157-158x). There is one other example, beyond the present study, of this asymmetry in high-GC actinobacteria where 4mC is partial and 6mA is complete.

Function class: M1-F1 Genome defence / evolutionary trace
Candidate function: Avoidance of the recognition sequence in the genome is detectable as the trace of past or present restriction pressure
Evidence: **[2026-10-06 Supported → Rejected]** The observation of depletion is established, but the hypothesis that it is a trace of restriction pressure was rejected from three directions (phage avoidance, REBASE correspondence, cross-genus panel; see below). Depletion is a property of high-GC actinobacteria as a whole, and the sister genus Kitasatospora, which has almost the same GC content, is depleted more strongly. Therefore this hypothesis is not supported. Depletion as an observation is retained in R11, but the explanation of restriction pressure is not used. 833-genome maximal-order Markov O/E: AAGCCCG 0.703 (73% below 0.75) versus HAAGCCCG 1.158 (833/833 above 1) versus TGGCCGGC 1.095 (820/833). Wilcoxon V=0, p=5.74e-138. Under the synonymous-substitution null, TGGCCGGC O/E is 0.721 / AAGCCCG is 0.837, both depleted. Under the within-M145 Markov, TGGCCGGC CDS is enriched at 1.173 → TGGCCGGC is dependent on an unresolved null. REBASE correspondence is rejected (the O/E is higher on the possessing side, it vanishes under GC control, and statistical power is not established because the positive control did not hold).**[2026-10-06 Addendum: phage-avoidance test]** **Streptomyces phages avoid neither of the two motifs.** 3,225 NCBI complete viral genomes (469 Streptomyces phages / 2,756 Mycobacterium phages) were reduced to 462 clusters at 16-mer FracMinHash Jaccard >= 0.25 and tested at the cluster level. Pooled maximal-order Markov O/E and percentile among control k-mers (50 non-palindromic k-mers of the same length and same GC count): in Streptomyces phages, TGGCCGGC 1.086 (80th percentile), AAGCCCG 1.022 (66). If restriction pressure were acting, the value should fall on the depleted side, but the observation is on the opposite side. **There is no host specificity either**: the only motif that is depleted, GAAGCCCG, is more strongly depleted in Mycobacterium phages, which do not use Streptomyces as a host (0.831 versus 0.894, Mann-Whitney BH q=1.2e-04). This should be interpreted as a compositional property common to high-GC phage genomes. **HAAGCCCG is consistently in excess (96-98th percentile) both in the host and in phages of the two genera** — what is new is that the separation seen across the 833 genomes (AAGCCCG 0.703 / HAAGCCCG 1.158) is reproduced in phage groups that do not share a host. TGGCCGGC appears strongly depleted under a 3rd-order Markov model (0.530 / 0.394), but because this disappears at the maximal order, it must not be written up as 'avoided'. Limits of this rejection: the absence of avoidance is not a sufficient condition for the absence of restriction pressure (extant phages can escape it through anti-restriction or self-methylation). There is isolation bias (skewed towards isolates on the S. lividans JI 1326 host). This is not a test restricted to phages that actually infect M145.**[2026-10-06 Cross-genus panel]** 290 genomes from 8 genera were obtained from NCBI RefSeq complete genomes and O/E was calculated with the same code. AAGCCCG O/E median: Bacillus 1.061 (GC 36.5%) / Escherichia 0.970 (50.6) / Corynebacterium 0.907 (60.0) / Mycobacterium 0.816 (66.7) / Rhodococcus 0.820 (67.3) / Nocardia 0.742 (68.1) / Amycolatopsis 0.748 (70.7) / Streptomyces 0.795 (71.7) / Kitasatospora 0.734 (73.0). In a regression across the 290 cross-genus genomes, GC explains 77% of the variance in O/E (slope -0.00985 / 1% GC, p=5.3e-94). Against the observed Streptomyces value of 0.7947, the GC-based prediction is 0.7545, a residual of +0.0397 (+0.74 times the cross-genus residual SD), so depletion is if anything weaker. The sister genus Kitasatospora, with almost the same GC content, is 0.7345, more strongly depleted than Streptomyces (Mann-Whitney p=8.2e-8). The GC dependence also remains in phylogenetically independent contrasts (200 representative genomes, an NJ tree from a 7,796-column rpoB+gyrB+recA+atpD+dnaN concatenation, 199 contrasts) (r=-0.384, p=2.3e-8, slope -0.0135 / 1% GC). → **Depletion is a property of high-GC actinobacteria as a whole and is not specific to Streptomyces.** HAAGCCCG has a median > 1 in all 8 genera (including Bacillus 1.052 / Escherichia 1.054). The Streptomyces residual is also +0.0136 (+0.18 SD). 'The enzyme's true target is not avoided' holds across genera. The Streptomyces residual for TGGCCGGC is -0.0486 (-0.49 SD), on the more depleted side relative to the GC prediction. Limitation: the maximal-order Markov model controls for GC and low-order composition but does not control for higher-order structure in 7-mer composition, so 'explicable by GC' should be read as 'explicable by compositional factors correlated with GC', and this does not assert that GC is the mechanism.

Evidence: The arrangement in which an orphan PglX lies near a DUF262 and a transposase suggests a mobile-element origin (this concerns PglX). The neighbouring HNH near SC_RS17645 is not co-expressed (rho=0.500, p=0.17. Positive controls: PglW-PglX rho=0.800 p=0.0096, SC_RS28835-SC_RS28845 rho=0.833 p=0.0053). **[2026-10-06 Rejected. SC_RS17645 has not been horizontally transferred]** (1) Composition is entirely native: GC3 93.68% is exactly the genome median (47.9th percentile among 7,508 genes, z=+0.25). GC3 is the indicator most sensitive to amelioration of foreign genes, and if this is native then recent horizontal transfer is rejected. Gene GC 77.50% (95.6th percentile) is skewed toward the high-GC side, the opposite direction from the classic HGT signature of a low-GC donor origin. Codon-usage RMSD 0.7467 (85.4th percentile) is likewise not an outlier. (2) The lineage is vertical: for the representative 200 genomes, the Mantel test gives Pearson r=0.607 / Spearman rho=0.624, with 999 permutations p=0.001 (120 shared taxa, 7,140 pairs). The normalised Robinson-Foulds distance of 0.735 reflects the low resolution of a single-gene NJ tree and cannot be interpreted on its own. (3) Among the 48 CDSs within +-25 kb of the neighbourhood, there are 0 instances of transposase / integrase / recombinase / phage / IS / conjugation / relaxase / resolvase. The neighbourhood consists of core metabolism such as enolase, RpfA/RpfC, a transcription-repair coupling factor, ribosomal protein L25 and PRPP synthetase. → The 55-57% carriage rate is the result of lineage-specific gene loss rather than the scattering of a selfish element.

Function class: M0a-F6 No function / neutrality of an orphan methyltransferase
Candidate function: The methyltransferase is an orphan with no cognate effector, and the methylome is a by-product with no functional consequence
Evidence: **[2026-10-06 Retraction. F1 ('a functionless molecular remnant') does not hold]** In molecular evolutionary analysis of 833 genomes (PAML yn00, YN00 method, icode=10), SC_RS17645 has omega = 0.0625 (n=144, IQR 0.0556-0.0802), 1/16 of neutral (omega=1). The housekeeping controls are gyrB 0.0281 / recA 0.0306 / rpoB 0.0343 / dnaN 0.0356 / atpD 0.0373; this enzyme is about twice as relaxed as those, but after BH correction it is significantly different from all controls at q < 4e-23. This is strong purifying selection. Three independent lines of evidence point in the same direction: (2) the non-canonical HPPF of catalytic motif IV is conserved in 457 of 472 orthologues (96.8%) across the whole genus (only 2 reverted to the canonical [SDN]PP[YF]). (3) The specificity-determining region TRD (539-669) is under the strongest constraint — omega 0.0411 versus catalytic motif IV 0.0640 (within-genome paired Wilcoxon n=272, p=3.7e-26), versus the MTase core 0.0786 (n=259, p=9.2e-33). The reverse of 'catalysis is preserved while specificity has degraded': the recognition sequence is being actively maintained. (4) Pseudogenisation is rare (frameshift 15/472 = 3.2%, premature stop 11/472 = 2.3%). The substance of 'non-possession' is complete deletion in 145 and possession of only a paralogue in 173 — not an intermediate stage of neutral decay. The neutral control was bimodal, and no calibrated neutral rate was obtained (median omega 2.96 across 463 both-lineage-collapsed pairs, falling to 0.081 under a strict filter — a selection bias). However, it has been confirmed that the pipeline can return omega > 1 for non-coding sequence (69.8% of both-lineage-collapsed pairs have omega > 0.5), so 0.0625 is not a methodological floor. The dS saturation rate is 68%, and since saturation causes omega to be overestimated, the true omega is likely even lower.

Evidence: **[2026-10-06 Chemical premise conflicts with the literature]**The initially established premise '4mC's deamination product is uracil, repaired by Ung' is incorrect. Chem Sci 2022 (doi:10.1039/d2sc02446b, full text confirmed via PMC) reports that cytosine and 5mC are deaminated by APOBEC3A to yield U and T, whereas 4mC resists deamination and is read as C. The direction is the same as the hypothesis (4mC is less mutagenic), but the mechanism differs. Moreover, there is prior work (Ehrlich M, Wilson GG, Kuo KC, Gehrke CW, J Bacteriol 1987;169(3):939-943, authors confirmed via Crossref). Test result: within the phylum, there is a relationship whereby higher GC is associated with the 4mC type, but the effect size is small (pooled OR 1.69 / +10% GC, CI lower bound 1.029 with genus-cluster-robust SE), and only Pseudomonadota passes BH on its own (OR 1.680 [1.304-2.164] q=2.4e-4). Actinomycetota, to which this bacterium belongs, is Undecidable with these data: OR 2.550 [0.843-7.713] q=0.130, n=65. Power was quantified by 600 simulations: even if the observed point estimate OR=2.55 is true, power is 37%, and at the pooled value of 1.69 it is 16%; an OR of about 4.5 is needed to reach 80%. Of the 374 records excluded for unknown GC, only 2 were Actinomycetota, and the loss from 79 records to 65 organisms is also minor, so this is a structural limitation that neither improved matching nor a mixed-effects model can recover from. A competing explanation remains viable: thermophilic genera show 4mC 22 versus 5mC 5, while non-thermophilic genera show 447 versus 572 (Fisher OR 5.63, p=1.1e-4). In a model including both thermophily and GC simultaneously, both remain: thermophily OR 3.637 [1.229-10.762], GC OR 1.665 [1.363-2.035]. The presence of Ung satisfies the premise but does not constitute evidence: M145 has 3 copies of UDG, and ung (SC_RS08680) is at 161.22 TPM at T1, but Ung is present in 1,122 of 1,123 genomes and is invariant across the 25-60% identity threshold. The presence of a universal gene does not distinguish between 4mC and 5mC. Furthermore, M145 also carries Mug (T:G repair) at 116.56 TPM at T1, and 90.0% of the genus panel carries it, so the latter half of the premise, that '5mC-derived T is not repaired,' also does not hold. The genus-wide CpG signature test is likewise Undecidable with these data: Streptomyces CpG shows a median O/E of 1.134, which is already in excess, so there is no depletion to explain and the test has no power to reject. A usable precedent: in Deinococcus radiodurans, 4mC (not 5mC) is the major modification, with 1,586 sites, 564 on CCGCGG, and a within-motif average of 70.0%. The configuration is almost identical to the present study, and since it is not a thermophile, an exception to the '4mC = thermophile modification' framework already exists.

Evidence: **[2026-10-06 New; approaching resolution with the out-of-genus panel]** Depletion of AAGCCCG is a uniform DNA-level bias that does not depend on reading frame, strand, coding/non-coding status, compartment, expression level, or mobile-element status, and both H-restriction and H-translation are Rejected. The depletion appears abruptly at 7 bp; all partial words are either enriched or neutral (AAGCC 1.2807 / AAGCCC 1.0902 / AGCCCG 1.0882 / GCCCG 0.9325 → AAGCCCG 0.7799). When measured with the same code across 8 out-of-genus genera and 290 genomes, GC explains 77% of the variance in AAGCCCG O/E (slope -0.00985 / 1% GC, p=5.3e-94). Against the observed value of 0.7947 for Streptomyces, the GC-based prediction is 0.7545, giving a residual of +0.0397 (+0.74 SD) — the depletion is weaker than predicted. The sister genus Kitasatospora, with almost the same GC (GC 73.0%), is 0.7345, showing stronger depletion than Streptomyces (Mann-Whitney p=8.2e-8). The GC dependence also remains in phylogenetically independent contrasts (200 representative genomes, 199 contrasts) (r=-0.384, p=2.3e-8), so this is a relationship realised repeatedly across the phylogenetic tree rather than inheritance from a single ancestral event. → The depletion is a property of high-GC Actinobacteria as a whole, and reduces to either mutation bias or compositional constraint. **Deciding between the two requires mutation-accumulation lines, and this cannot be tested with the data of this project.** The maximal-order Markov model controls for GC and low-order composition but does not control for higher-order structure in 7-mer composition, so 'explicable by GC' should be read as 'explicable by compositional factors correlated with GC'. TGGCCGGC is explained by codon composition and so is Out of scope for this organism.
